List the matings of a pedigree

Source: R/getMatings.R
getMatings.Rd

A mating is a sire and a dam with at least one offspring recorded with both of them, or a pair declared mated in matings. getMatings() lists each mating once: first those with offspring, in the order the first offspring of each comes in ped, with the number of offspring the two share; then each declared pair with no offspring together, in the order of matings, with 0. These are the matings a drawing of the pedigree draws, in its order (makePedigreeMatingLayout, given the same matings). An animal's mates are the animals it is listed with.

Usage

getMatings(ped, matings = NULL)

Arguments

ped

a data frame with the columns id, sire and dam, an unknown parent written NA (see recodePedigree). Factor columns are read by their labels and numbers as text.

matings

NULL (the default) or a data frame with the columns sire and dam (text or factor; other columns are ignored), one row per mating declared whether or not the two have offspring together, as makePedigreeMatingLayout takes it. Stops on anything but NULL or a data frame with both columns, on NA, and on the same id as sire and dam.

Value

A data frame with one row per mating and the columns sire and dam (text) and offspring (an integer, the number of animals with that sire and dam; 0 for a declared mating with none). It has no rows when no animal has both parents known and no mating is declared.

Details

An offspring with only one known parent makes no mating (its parent's countOffspring counts it). A sire or dam with no row of its own is listed as recorded. Each offspring is counted once.

A row of matings naming a pair with offspring together, in either column, adds nothing and gives no message, so the result of getMatings() can be passed back, with rows added. A pair named twice, in either column, is listed once, as its first row names it; the sexes are not checked. A row naming an animal without a row of its own in ped, as a trimming function leaves, is left out, with a message naming the pair, as the drawing leaves it out.

See also

countOffspring, getOffspring

Examples

## A and B have C; A and E have F; A has G, its dam unknown; B has H,
## its sire unknown; K and E have I.
ped <- data.frame(
  id = c("A", "B", "E", "K", "C", "F", "G", "H", "I"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, "A", "A", "A", NA, "K"),
  dam = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, "B", "E", NA, "B", "E")
)
matings <- getMatings(ped)
matings
#>   sire dam offspring
#> 1    A   B         1
#> 2    A   E         1
#> 3    K   E         1
## The mates of E.
c(matings$dam[matings$sire == "E"], matings$sire[matings$dam == "E"])
#> [1] "A" "K"
## K and B declared mated, with no offspring together.
getMatings(ped, matings = data.frame(sire = "K", dam = "B"))
#>   sire dam offspring
#> 1    A   B         1
#> 2    A   E         1
#> 3    K   E         1
#> 4    K   B         0
